newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net reserves, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its international reserves as of May 30 were $22.262 billion, compared to $22.181 billion on May 23.
The central bank said that its net international assets as of the same date rose to $14.442 billion from $13.533 billion the week before.
The central bank said the increase of $909 million in net international assets during the period was due to:
--Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $730 million.
--Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $158 million.

--A net gain of $21 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that the monetary base rose 3.755 billion pesos due to a rise in the seasonal demand of bills and coins and other factors.
It said the deposits of FOBAPROA fell 3.493 billion pesos, while deposits of the federal government rose 622 million pesos.
The central bank said the increase in FOBAPROA deposits meant the Banco de Mexico only had to undertake monetary operations to sterilize funds worth 187 million pesos.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
May 23 May 30
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $22.181 bln $22.262 bln
Monetary Base 76.929 80.684
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $13.533 bln $14.442 bln
Net Domestic Credit -29.616 -33.647
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
((--Robert Kozak, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7902))
